__comment__: TypeThatBook index + TTL definitions. v2.0.0 (2026-08-02).
This file is the ONLY machine-readable record of what is configured in the
console. Jake has no CLI, so nothing here is applied by deploying it - it is
documentation that happens to be valid JSON. Every entry must be created by
hand: composite indexes in the Firebase console (Firestore > Indexes), TTL
policies and single-field exemptions in the GOOGLE CLOUD console.
WHY THE EXEMPTIONS MATTER, since they are new in v2.0.0:
Firestore automatically builds an ascending AND a descending index for every
field of every document, and index storage is billed the same as document
storage. typing_logs is the collection that grows fastest - one document per
student per school day, so roughly 1.26 million documents a year at full
district scale - and most of its fields are never used in a where() or an
orderBy() anywhere in the codebase. They are payload, read back with the
document, and indexing them buys nothing and costs storage forever.
Verified by grep across game.js, learn.js, reports.html and lessons-admin.js
on 2026-08-02: the ONLY typing_logs fields ever queried are classId, schoolId
and date. Everything else below is exempt.
TTL NOTE: typing_sessions and practice_sessions carry expiresAt and are
collected at 120 days - Jake confirmed both policies are live. typing_logs
deliberately has NO TTL: it is the collection reports grade from, it is small
per document, and losing a year of it would lose a year of records. The
exemptions below are what keep its storage growth flat instead of linear in
field count. Revisit only if storage becomes the binding constraint.
